rubriker.title: The Chess Olympiad that wasn't: Munich 1936
rubriker._rss_content: Among all the Chess Olympiads held throughout history, the 1936 tournament in Munich occupies a special place. FIDE did not officially recognise the event as a Chess Olympiad. Nevertheless, the competition between national teams met all the requirements. Like in 2026, the German team also won the bronze medal on this occasion. | Photos: Ferenc Chalupetzky / Tournament Book

rubriker.title: U.S. Championship: Round 2
rubriker._rss_content: Round 2 in Saint Louis on Saturday cut the open section's leaders from three to two, with Wesley So surviving a bad position against Jeffery Xiong and Awonder Liang beating Samuel Sevian, while Fabiano Caruana scored his first win to move within half a point. In the women's section, Megan Paragua and Thalia Cervantes, the two lowest-rated players in the field, took the lead at 2/2, with Paragua beating defending champion Carissa Yip.
